$description: The design language of spec-10 Annex A, in the Design Tokens Format Module 2025.10. This file is the default resolution: theme dark, distance near, density comfortable, contrast normal, motion full. Every other context is an override file under contexts/, named by resolver.json. Annex A holds that every value here is a starting value maintained as spec-10 §20's registry, so disagreeing with one is a registry change rather than a change to the annex; each value derived rather than read off the annex records its derivation.

base.$description: A.1.4's primitive tier: raw values carrying no meaning, referencing nothing. A primitive exists here where more than one role shares it, or where a scale is computed from one step. Everything else is authored once at sys, which is what the annex itself does.

space.$description: A.4.1: a 4px base with an 8px rhythm, linear, computed from one base value rather than enumerated, so a density or distance change is one number. In rem because A.1.3 admits px only for the four primitives it closes the set on.

100.$description: 8px. The rhythm, and the minimum separation between two undersized targets.

200.$description: 16px. A card's inset, and the page's minimum side gutter.

1200.$description: 96px. The safe inset's horizontal value at distance far on a 1920-wide canvas.

grey.$description: A.2.2's twelve-step ramp at one hue. Steps 01 to 05 are also A.6's elevation scale; 06 to 08 are the border scale. Authored in OKLCH with an sRGB fallback, neither computed by the build (A.2.1); colour_test.exs asserts the two agree. Step 01 is not pure black and step 12 is not pure white (A.2.3): a black page leaves no room to express elevation downward, and maximal light-on-dark contrast blooms, worst for uncorrected astigmatism.

02.$description: Subtle background. The ground every contrast figure in A.2 is measured against.

05.$description: Component background, active or selected. Also elevation: overlay.

11.$description: Low-contrast text. 8.46:1 on step 02, APCA Lc 60.5 — which clears A.2.4's Lc 60 secondary floor and not its Lc 75 body floor, so this is secondary text and never body text.

12.$description: High-contrast text. 15.13:1 on step 02, APCA Lc 95.4.

ring.$description: Not a ramp step (A.2.2). One primitive shared by the focus ring and by a significant boundary, because A.6 requires a boundary to clear 3:1 and no ramp step does: this clears 5.17:1 at step 01 falling to 3.68:1 at step 05.

hue.$description: A.2.6's class colours, all at one OKLCH lightness so measured contrast holds roughly constant across them: all five span 6.58:1 to 7.53:1 against step 02 and every pair is at least 134 rgb units apart. Six classes, five colours — sRGB at this lightness has room for a fifth hue and not a sixth, so package shares text's rose and A.8.6's glyph carries the difference.

video.$description: Indigo. Film, television episode, home video.

audio.$description: Amber. Music recording, audiobook, podcast episode.

software.$description: Green. Video game. A hue of its own because nothing else in the catalog is run rather than read, heard or watched.

solid.$description: The readable foreground on any saturated solid. One ink serves the class colours and the status colours both: measured against all nine solids it beats white under WCAG 2 in every case, reaching 6.66:1 on the least contrasting class colour and 4.54:1 on the least contrasting status colour.

signal.$description: The four status solids. Each requires a non-colour carrier as well (spec-10 §17.9), so none is the sole carrier of a state. Measured with base.ink.solid these reach WCAG 2 ratios of 4.54, 11.26, 5.63 and 7.07 but APCA Lc of only 37.2, 76.2, 44.3 and 53.4, so a status solid carries a glyph or a short label and never body text, which A.2.4's Lc 75 floor would refuse.

sys.$description: A.1.4's semantic tier: roles, and the only tier templates, component code and component styles may reference. A component reaching into base means the semantic layer is inadequate and the answer is to add a role. A.11 makes these names the public interface, so renaming one is a breaking change; the emphasis vocabulary is subtle / bare / strong / solid and is one of the three decisions A.11 calls most expensive to reverse.

surface.$description: The ground a region sits on, as against a fill, which is the background of something a person operates. A.1.5 rule 1 forbids a name carrying a state, so no surface is named for being hovered: the emphasis is in the name and the state is in the selector.

subtle.$description: A region set back from the page without being raised off it. Also the ground every contrast figure in A.2 is measured against.

raised.$description: A card, a shelf tile. A tonal step alone is 1.10:1 against the base and cannot carry a boundary, so a raised surface whose edge is functionally significant also carries sys.color.border.strong.

fill.$description:
The background of something a person operates. A.2.6 spends saturation only on the class and status colours, so a control is built from the ramp: A.11's emphasis ladder — subtle, bare, strong, solid — is what distinguishes the rungs, and a state is expressed by choosing a rung in a selector rather than by a name.

The last segment is hyphenated rather than nested because a token cannot both hold a value and contain another: `fill.subtle` and `fill.subtle-strong` are siblings.

subtle.$description: A control at rest. With sys.color.on.surface.strong this reaches 13.71:1 in the dark theme and 14.41:1 in the light one, which is why a text-bearing control is built from this rung and not from a solid.

solid.$description: A control carrying its own weight: a filled badge, a meter, a selected chip. Not a body-text background — see sys.color.on.fill.

strong.$description: Body and heading text. Lc 95.4 on step 02, clearing A.2.4's Lc 75 body floor.

muted.$description: Secondary text, captions, and the words an absence is stated in. Lc 60.5, which clears the secondary floor and not the body floor.

class.$description: A token rather than a constant because a solid's readable foreground varies by hue; at one lightness it does not have to, which is what the token absorbs when a class is added at another.

fill.$description:
The ink on a solid fill. It references the ramp's text end, so it follows the theme: light in the dark theme and dark in the light one.

Measured, a grey solid is not a body-text background. On sys.color.fill.solid it reaches 4.27:1 in the dark theme and 4.96:1 in the light, and on the engaged rung 3.41:1 and 4.33:1 — every one of which clears WCAG 2 §1.4.11's 3:1 for non-text and §1.4.3's 3:1 for large text, and none of which reliably clears 4.5:1 for body text. That is the midpoint of any neutral ramp and not a fault in this one. A control bearing body text uses sys.color.fill.subtle instead.

component-strong.$description: That edge engaged. Hyphenated rather than nested because a token cannot both hold a value and contain another.

strong.$description: A functionally significant boundary. A.6 makes the obligation the 3:1 ratio rather than the step, and no border step reaches it against any surface, so this resolves to the ring's primitive. A role of its own rather than a reference to the focus ring because A.2.7 rebinds the semantic tier to system colour keywords in defined pairs: a boundary binds to ButtonBorder and a focus indicator to Highlight, and one name cannot be both.

ring.$description: Drawn with outline and never box-shadow, which computes to none under forced colours — a shadow-only ring vanishes for exactly the people most likely to be in that mode.

package.$description: Shares text's rose, because a comic issue is read a page at a time on the reader a document and an ebook get. The name exists separately so a release finding a sixth hue worth spending gives package a value and touches no template.

type.$description: A.3.1's one modular scale at roughly 1.2 in the interface range, authored to whole pixels and widening for display sizes. The ratio is held constant across contexts and only the base moves, which is why every size here is in rem and the distance switch changes the root rather than this table. A.3.2 bounds any fluid size at 2.5 times its minimum.

sans.$description: The interface face. Roboto Flex carries a variable optical-size axis, which is what lets A.3.5's rule be honoured rather than recorded as a limitation.

serif.$description: Long-form reading and a scan's transcript.

mono.$description: A timecode, a digest, a page position.

caption.$description: 12px at near. Metadata under a tile, and forbidden as body text on a television surface.

md.$description: 16px at near, 32px at far by a root-size switch rather than a second ramp.

reading.$description: 18px. Long-form text, constrained to the measure, with every attribute adjustable by the reader (A.3.6).

data.$description: 13px. Tabular figures wherever digits line up.

leading.$description: Line height as a multiplier of font size, one per style. Held apart from sys.type rather than composed with it, because the format's typography composite requires all five of fontFamily, fontSize, fontWeight, letterSpacing and lineHeight, and the annex supplies no letter spacing — A.1.2 forbids smuggling a value in to satisfy a schema. A.3.6 supplies two of these, body 1.55 and display 1.15, and requires a reader be able to set line height.

sm.$description: A.3.6's own figure, which it gives for every display size.

reading.$description: Looser than body, because long-form reading is the one surface a line's return sweep is repeated on.

weight.$description: A.3.5 requires the weight be raised one step at distance far and names no weights, so these three are the household's own. Roboto Flex carries a variable weight axis, so a step is continuous rather than a separate file.

medium.$description: Titles, and display below the largest.

target.$description: A.4.2's four floors, stated separately because conflating them ships 24px buttons described as conformant. In rem so a root-size change at distance far doubles them without a second token set.

min.$description: 24px. WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8's conformance floor, or its 24px-circle spacing exception. A legal floor, not a design target.

remote.$description: 56px near, 112px at far. A directional remote. No television platform publishes a minimum focusable size, so this is derived from A.3.3's angular requirement and A.4.4's focus-scale headroom.

height.$description: 48px, which is exactly sys.size.target.touch: the interface has to be thumb-operable on a phone at comfortable density. Derived rather than read from the annex, which requires density to change control height and names no token for it. Density lowers it to 40px, and A.1.6 forbids going below A.4.2's 24px floor.

radius.$description: Modest throughout: poster art and scans are rectangular, and a large radius crops the content it frames.

md.$description: 8px. A button, a tile, a card.

full.$description: A pill: a facet chip, a status badge. One of the four px primitives A.1.3 closes the set on, because A.1.2's admissible units cannot express a pill as a proportion.

hairline.$description: A separator. A fixed thinness rather than a proportion of the type size, which is why A.1.3 permits px here.

component.$description: A control's edge. Survives three metres where a 1.10:1 tone step does not.

width.$description: 2px at near and 4px at far, which falls out of the root-size switch and needs no fifth px primitive.

duration.$description: A.7 adopts Material 3's published set whole.

focus-move.$description: Focus travelling between two elements. Shorter at far rather than longer, because focus on a remote moves repeatedly and in sequence so per-move duration accumulates into felt latency.
